summary: Feed s143_double to IDS is degraded: 50% of packets are untagged and required VLAN 20 is completely missing, plus IDS port is overloaded by microbursts to 1.53 Gbps on a 1 Gbps port (153% capacity). IDS has incomplete visibility and will drop traffic during bursts.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker or upstream trunk is stripping 802.1Q tags or not forwarding VLAN 20. IDS requires VLANs 10 and 20 but 50% of packets arrive untagged and VLAN 20 is never observed, indicating tag stripping or VLAN pruning on the broker/switch.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS is blind to VLAN 20 and to half of all traffic; signatures, anomaly detection and correlation for that segment never fire, creating a major detection coverage gap.

recommended_fix.why: Restore and preserve 802.1Q tags end-to-end so the IDS receives both required VLANs 10 and 20 for complete coverage

findings.root_cause: Traffic microbursts peak at 1.53 Gbps in 1ms intervals, exceeding the 1 Gbps IDS port by 53% across 5 intervals. No load-balancing or buffering in front of the tool to absorb bursts.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS ingress buffers overflow and drops packets during bursts; TCP reassembly breaks, IDS signatures miss attacks, and stateful detection degrades or fails open under load.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across 2x 1 Gbps IDS ports/instances via packet broker load-balancing to keep per-port utilization below 80% and prevent burst drops
